operating_system_subtitle: Real-time operating system for microcontrollers and small microprocessors
operating_system_description: FreeRTOS is a market-leading embedded system RTOS supporting 40+ processor architectures with a small memory footprint, fast execution times, and cutting-edge RTOS features and libraries including Symmetric Multiprocessing (SMP), a thread-safe TCP stack with IPv6 support, and seamless integration with cloud services. It’s open-source and actively supported and maintained.
features_description: Distributed freely under the MIT open source license, FreeRTOS includes a kernel and a growing set of libraries suitable for use across all industry sectors. FreeRTOS is built with an emphasis on reliability and ease of use.
trusted_kernel_desc: With proven robustness, tiny footprint, and wide device support, the FreeRTOS kernel is trusted by world-leading companies as the de facto standard for microcontrollers and small microprocessors.
acc_time_desc: With detailed pre-configured demos and Internet of Things (IoT) reference integrations, there is no need to determine how to setup a project. Quickly download, compile, and get to market faster.
support_for_desc: One code base for <Link to="/Documentation/02-Kernel/03-Supported-devices/00-Supported-devices">40+ MCU architectures</Link> and 15+ toolchains, including the latest RISC-V and ARMv8-M (Arm Cortex-M33) microcontrollers
broad_partnership_desc: Our <Link to="/Partners">partner ecosystem</Link> provides a breadth of options including community contributions, professional support, as well as integrated IDE and productivity tools.
open_source_desc: Open source for 20 years, FreeRTOS can be used for any purpose under its <Link to="/Documentation/02-Kernel/01-About-the-FreeRTOS-kernel/04-Licensing">MIT license</Link>. Our strategic partner also provides <Link target="_blank" to="/Documentation/02-Kernel/01-About-the-FreeRTOS-kernel/04-Licensing#optional-freertos-commercial-licensing">commercial licenses</Link>, and safety <Link to="/Partners/Safety">certification</Link>.
long_term_support_desc: FreeRTOS offers feature stability with <Link to="/Documentation/03-Libraries/01-Library-overview/03-LTS-libraries/01-LTS-libraries">long term support (LTS)</Link> releases. FreeRTOS LTS libraries come with security updates and critical bug fixes for two years. Maintained by AWS for the benefit of the FreeRTOS community.
learn_freertos_desc: The FreeRTOS beginners’ guide will help you understand the RTOS concept, use cases and extended features. It will also help you get started with your first project with demos and tutorials.
partners_desc: FreeRTOS partners with semiconductor manufacturers to jointly provide reference implementations for specific microcontrollers and microprocessors. The reference implementations are usually provided in the semiconductor partner's tool chain.
stay_on_top: Stay on top of the new releases, features, and events

professional_team_desc: With our team of experts by your side, you'll never have to go it alone on your journey to success. Our team is dedicated to providing you with the support, guidance, and resources you need to achieve your goals, no matter how big or small. From one-on-one coaching and personalized advice, to access to a community of like-minded individuals, we've got you covered.
architecture_description: FreeRTOS partners with companies and organizations providing Instruction Set Architectures (ISA) and Intellectual Property (IP) to semiconductor firms. FreeRTOS Kernel Ports align with architectures to provide broad ecosystem support.
semiconductor_description: FreeRTOS partners with semiconductor manufacturers to jointly provide reference implementations for specific microcontrollers and microprocessors. The reference implementations are usually provided in the semiconductor partner's tool chain.
productivity_description: FreeRTOS partners with development tools and hardware kit manufacturers that provide incredible value to developers building on FreeRTOS. Development tools and kits are essential to get projects off the ground and accelerate productivity through rapid prototyping and enhanced debugging. In some cases, the tools can be actively used in production workload contexts.
training_description: FreeRTOS partners with training firms to help get your product teams and individuals building on FreeRTOS up to speed on FreeRTOS development quickly and in a structured way. FreeRTOS partners with consulting firms to help get your embedded developers jump-started in the right direction or even deliver your entire product built on FreeRTOS.
software_description: FreeRTOS partners with Independent Software Vendors (ISVs) to provide entire software libraries that enable turnkey functionality in your project and entire FreeRTOS licensed or industry tested packaged distributions.
bsp_description: FreeRTOS is the market leading RTOS solution for microcontrollers, and as such, many manufacturers provide low level drivers and higher level middleware that is pre-packaged or pre-integrated with FreeRTOS.
FreeRTOS_Raspberry_Pi: Using FreeRTOS with the Raspberry Pi Pico
embedded_applications: In this blog series, we will explore writing embedded applications for the Raspberry Pi Pico using FreeRTOS.
symmetric_multiprocessing: Symmetric Multiprocessing (SMP) with FreeRTOS and Raspberry Pi Pico
smp_support: SMP support in the FreeRTOS Kernel enables one instance of the FreeRTOS kernel to schedule tasks across multiple identical processor cores, which can be helpful for embedded applications in areas like IoT. This session will showcase the FreeRTOS Raspberry Pi Pico port to demonstrate support for SMP in the FreeRTOS Kernel.
risc_v: Building Applications with RISC-V and FreeRTOS
get_the_skills: Get the skills that enable you to build embedded systems with RTOS capabilities for real-time applications.
modernize_applications: Are you planning to use the Internet of Things (IoT) to modernize industrial applications, ship new consumer products faster, or reinvent smart buildings and cities? With AWS IoT ExpressLink, you can quickly and easily develop cloud connected devices, starting with a hardware module powered by AWS IoT ExpressLink.

presentation_by: Presentation by Richard Barry at AWS on June 12, 2019 at the RISC-V Workshop Zurich at ETH Zurich in Zurich, Switzerland.
innovation_coffee_desc: Watch Innovation Coffee on-demand with Richard Barry, Senior Principal Engineer at AWS and Founder of FreeRTOS to see how to develop applications in the cloud using Arm tools and FreeRTOS.

stanmoy.name: Tanmoy Sen
stanmoy.title: Product manager
stanmoy.description: Tanmoy Sen is a Senior Product Manager at Amazon Web Services where he focuses on helping customers and embedded developers connect microcontroller-based devices to the cloud.

luciodj.name: Lucio Di Jasio
luciodj.title: Product manager
luciodj.description: Lucio is a Product Manager at Amazon Web Services. He has held various technical and marketing roles in the semiconductor industry for the past 20 years. As an opinionated and prolific author he has published numerous articles and technical books on programming for embedded control applications. Following his passion for flying, he has achieved both FAA and EASA private pilot licenses.

lesau.name: Victor Lesau
lesau.title: Senior Product Manager
lesau.description: Victor is a Product Manager at Amazon Web Services (AWS) IoT. Previously, he co-founded CuePath Innovation, a healthcare IoT startup with patented smart medication packaging technology, published embedded Linux research on reconfigurable FPGA systems, and engineered fiber optics products at Microsemi.

aggarg.name: Gaurav Aggarwal
aggarg.title: FreeRTOS kernel and embedded connectivity specialist
aggarg.description: Gaurav Aggarwal is a FreeRTOS kernel and embedded connectivity specialist within the IoT edge devices team at Amazon Web Services. He was instrumental in bringing both the ARM Cortex-M33 and Cortex-M23 FreeRTOS kernel ports to market, and now supports their use while also maintaining an active role in the development and enhancement of the FreeRTOS library portfolio.

ribarry.name: Richard Barry
ribarry.title: Founder of FreeRTOS
ribarry.description: Richard Barry founded the FreeRTOS project in 2003, spent more than a decade developing and promoting FreeRTOS through his company Real Time Engineers Ltd, and now continues his work on FreeRTOS within a larger team as a principal engineer at Amazon Web Services. Richard graduated with 1st Class Honors in Computing for Real Time Systems, and was awarded an Honorary Doctorate for his contributions to the development of embedded technology. Richard has also been directly involved in the startup of several companies, and authored several books.

mohameda.name: Mohamed Abdelmaksoud
mohameda.title: Embedded IoT engineer
mohameda.description: Mohamed Abdelmaksoud is an embedded IoT engineer at 1NCE where he focuses on designing and developing cellular IoT products. He's also conducting research on the optimization of energy and data consumption of constrained IoT devices with different IoT protocols and radio access technologies.

sam-tayloramazon-com.name: Sam Taylor
sam-tayloramazon-com.title: Senior director
sam-tayloramazon-com.description: Sam Taylor is Senior Director, IoT Software Strategy at Arm.

tony_smithtwilio-com.name: Tony Smith
tony_smithtwilio-com.title: Developer educator
tony_smithtwilio-com.description: Tony Smith is a Developer Educator at Twilio IoT. Previously, he was the Senior Tech Writer at IoT PaaS company Electric Imp, which was acquired by Twilio in 2019. He has spent more than 25 years as a journalist focusing on various aspects of the technology sector: channel, consumer, business, product development and research. His current areas of interest include the Internet of Things; the 'maker' world of DIY technology product development; and the history of British microcomputing.

wallit.name: Toshiyanger Walling
wallit.title: Software development manager
wallit.description: Toshiyanger Walling is a Software Development Manager on the FreeRTOS team at Amazon Web Services where he manages a team responsible for building and sustaining FreeRTOS software.

pvyawaha.name: Prasad Vyawahare
pvyawaha.title: Software development engineer
pvyawaha.description: Prasad is a Software Development Engineer at Amazon Web Services where he focuses on developing libraries to enable IoT connectivity for edge devices. Prior to AWS, he worked in developing low power network stacks and embedded software for in-vehicle infotainment systems , cellular modem and industrial analytical instruments.

kanherea.name: Aniruddha Kanhere
kanherea.title: Software development engineer
kanherea.description: Aniruddha is an Embedded Software Development Engineer at Amazon Web Services where he focuses on developing libraries such as FreeRTOS+TCP, coreMQTT, etc. to enable IoT connectivity for edge devices.

nnkamath.name: Nikhil Kamath
nnkamath.title: Software Development Manager
nnkamath.description: Nikhil Kamath is a Software Development Manager at AWS. He has held various positions ranging from Software Engineer to Engineering Manager over the past 15+ years in the technology industry. His experience spans multiple industry verticals including Internet of Things (IoT), industrial automation, medical devices , and in-flight entertainment systems.

arm-author.name: Shebu Varghese Kuriakose
arm-author.title: Director of software technology management
arm-author.description: Shebu Varghese Kuriakose is Director, Software Technology Management with Arm’s Open Source Software Group and Chairman of the Trusted Firmware Project Board. Shebu drives the Trusted Firmware-M development roadmap and collaboration with Silicon vendors, RTOS and Tools ecosystem.

gooddan.name: Dan Good
gooddan.title: Senior software development engineer
gooddan.description: Dan Good works as a Senior Software Development Engineer at Amazon Web Services. After a long career in networking, the thriving maker culture inspired him to dive in to IoT. Dan contributes to the FreeRTOS core* libraries and the AWS IoT SDK for embedded C to empower customers to innovate.

adamlewis.name: Adam Lewis
adamlewis.title: Embedded engineer
adamlewis.description: Adam Lewis is an embedded engineer on the SAFERTOS® development team at WITTENSTEIN high integrity systems.

elberger.name: Richard Elberger
elberger.title: IoT principal technologist
elberger.description: Richard Elberger is an IoT Principal Technologist at Amazon Web Services. As a prolific speaker, periodic writer, and tireless embedded technology addict, he creates content and builds community for IoT and Cloud practitioners globally. Richard maintains and contributes to multiple IoT-related open source projects (FreeRTOS, meta-aws, ThingPress) which helps customers build and deliver amazing IoT solutions on AWS.

francesca-finocchiaro.name: Francesca Finocchiaro
francesca-finocchiaro.title: Physicist & Project manager
francesca-finocchiaro.description: Francesca Finocchiaro, physicist by formation, holds a project manager role within eProsima. At present, she is leading the micro-ROS team and coordinating the EU project at OFERA (http://www.ofera.eu/external_link), which developed and actively maintains micro-ROS.

gvg.name: Gaurav Gupta
gvg.title: Global partner solutions architect
gvg.description: Gaurav Gupta is a Global Partner Solutions Architect at AWS IoT where he focuses on helping customers & partners, specifically IoT connectivity enablers in LoRaWAN and Telco, build and integrate their products with AWS services. Prior to AWS, he has 15+ years of experience in wireless standards, network architecture and deployment in tier-1 operator. He has 11 granted patents in wireless/IoT/cloud and several patents pending.

jacoblassen.name: Jacob Lunn Lassen
jacoblassen.title: Director of Atmel & Senior manager of Microchip
jacoblassen.description: Jacob Lunn Lassen has a M.Sc.EE. from Aalborg University in Denmark. He joined Atmel’s AVR Applications team in 2000, and worked with key customer support, motor control, smart batteries, EMC research and product development. He joined Microchip’s PIC and AVR MCUs marketing team in 2016, now working on product definition, IoT and Functional Safety.

marc-goodner.name: Marc Goodner
marc-goodner.title: Program manager
marc-goodner.description: Marc Goodner is a Program Manager on the C++ team at Microsoft working on improving embedded support in Visual Studio and Visual Studio Code.

ncchong.name: Nathan Chong
ncchong.title: Principal engineer
ncchong.description: Nathan Chong is a Principal Engineer with the Automated Reasoning Group at Amazon Web Services. His work focuses on the correctness of concurrent systems code, particularly at the hardware-software boundary.

talupur.name: Murali Talupur
talupur.title: Principal applied scientist
talupur.description: Murali Talupur is a Principal Applied Scientist with the Automated Reasoning Group at Amazon Web Services (AWS). His work focuses on formal verification of distributed systems and critical software libraries.

aismail.name: Ahmed Ismail
aismail.title: Software Engineer
aismail.description: Ahmed Ismail is a Software Engineer in IoT-Edge Software at Arm, where he focuses on developing FreeRTOS based Internet of Things (IoT) software stack along with AI based applications running on Arm's edge devices. He's also responsible for supporting Arm's latest architecture features in FreeRTOS-Kernel.

whats-new-1.title: Refactoring FreeRTOS for the next 20 years
whats-new-1.description: In this talk, we will explore the next 20 years with Amazon's involvement, including the technical roadmap, today's design, and distribution philosophy.
whats-new-1.author: Richard Barry

whats-new-2.title: Using future-proofed Microcontroller Designs with FreeRTOS
whats-new-2.description: In this session, discover how to overcome challenges in development acceleration while ensuring firmware integrity and longevity, how that ties into Long Term Support releases, and what that means for an open source project in development for more than 15 years.
whats-new-2.author: Richard Barry
